TX.name: Texas
TX.basis_note: Texas taxes the market value of oil, gas and condensate (the Comptroller's pages). Marketing costs: the Comptroller publishes an 'Audit Policy on Natural Gas Marketing Costs' that this page did not read, so no deduction is computed.

base.name: Oil production tax
base.quote: Oil production tax: 4.6 percent (.046) of market value of oil

code.quote: The tax imposed by this chapter is at the rate of 4.6 percent of the market value of oil produced in this state or 4.6 cents for each barrel of 42 standard gallons of oil produced in this state, whichever rate results in the greater amount of tax.

fees.name: Oil Field Clean-Up Fee
fees.quote: For report periods September 2015 and later, the taxable barrels are subject to the Oil Field Clean-Up Fee of $0.00625 (5/8 of a cent) per barrel

options.name: Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR), Exempt Type 05
options.who: Oil from an enhanced recovery project certified by the Texas Railroad Commission; a valid project number must be reported
options.what: The tax rate falls from 4.6 to 2.3 percent of market value
options.how_long: 10 years beginning the first day of the month after the Railroad Commission certifies a positive production response (or, for an expansion, incremental production)
options.quote: Enhanced Oil Recovery Exemption (EOR): 2.3 percent (.023) of market value of oil

code.quote: the recovered oil tax rate applies to oil on which a tax is imposed by this chapter for the 10 years beginning the first day of the month following the date the commission certifies that, in the case of an enhanced recovery project including a co-production project, a positive production response has occurred

options.name: EOR using anthropogenic carbon dioxide, Exempt Type 14

param.label: Additional reduction of the EOR rate, percent: 50 times the anthropogenic share of the CO2 used

options.who: An EOR project whose carbon dioxide is captured from an anthropogenic source in Texas, would otherwise be released, is measurable at capture, and is sequestered in Texas
options.what: Up to an additional 50 percent reduction of the tax rate (the calculator applies it to the EOR rate, 2.3 percent)
options.how_long: Until the 30th anniversary of the date the Comptroller first approves the application; the reduction is prorated to the anthropogenic share of the carbon dioxide used
options.quote: Up to an additional 50 percent reduction in the tax rate applies if in the recovery of the oil, the enhanced recovery project uses carbon dioxide that: is captured from an anthropogenic source in this state

code.quote: until the 30th anniversary of the date that the comptroller first approves an application for a tax rate reduction under this section, the producer of oil recovered through an enhanced oil recovery project that qualifies under Section 202.054 for the recovered oil tax rate provided by Section 202.052 (b) is entitled to an additional 50 percent reduction in that tax rate

options.name: Two-Year Inactive Well Exemption
options.who: Oil from a well certified by the Railroad Commission as a two-year inactive well
options.what: 0.0 percent of market value
options.how_long: Five years
options.quote: Two-Year Inactive Well Exemption: 0.0 percent (.000) of market value of oil

code.quote: Hydrocarbons produced from a well qualify for a five-year severance tax exemption if the commission designates the well as a two-year inactive well.

options.name: Low-producing oil lease credit, Exempt Type 11

tiers.label: Certified average oil price more than $30: no credit

options.who: An oil lease whose production over a 90-day period averages less than 15 barrels per well per day, or less than 5 percent recoverable oil per barrel of produced water; Form AP-216
options.what: A credit of 25, 50 or 100 percent of the tax, set by the Comptroller-certified average (in 2005 dollars) oil price for the report month (not the price entered here); it can combine with Types 05 and 14
options.how_long: Each report month, while the lease qualifies and by the certified price
options.quote: Average Taxable Oil Price Eligibility More than $30 No credit Over $25 to $30 25 percent credit Over $22 to to $25 50 percent credit $22 or less 100 percent credit

code.quote: Each month, the comptroller shall certify the average taxable price of oil, adjusted to 2005 dollars, during the previous three months

certified.note: The Comptroller-certified average taxable price by report period, in 2005 dollars, as the Comptroller's page publishes it. Rows inside an HTML comment on the page (September to December 2026, copied from 2025) are not published and are not here.

base.name: Natural gas production tax
base.quote: Gas: 7.5 percent (.075) of market value of gas.

code.quote: The tax imposed by this chapter is at the rate of 7.5 percent of the market value of gas produced and saved in this state by the producer.

fees.name: Oil-Field Cleanup Regulatory Fee on Natural Gas
fees.quote: Oil-Field Cleanup Regulatory Fee on Natural Gas of $.000667 (one fifteenth of a cent) per 1,000 cubic feet of gas

options.name: High-Cost Gas Reduced Tax Rate, Type 5

param.label: The well's drilling and completion costs as a multiple of the median for high-cost wells of the previous state fiscal year (1.0 is the median)

options.who: Gas from a gas well certified by the Railroad Commission; the rate depends on how the well's drilling and completion costs compare with the median cost of high-cost gas wells of the previous state fiscal year
options.what: The rate is 7.5 percent less 7.5 percent times the ratio of the well's drilling and completion costs to twice the median, never below zero: a well at the median pays 3.75 percent, one at twice the median or more pays nothing
options.how_long: The first 120 consecutive calendar months from first production, or until the cumulative reduction equals 50 percent of the drilling and completion costs, whichever occurs first (wells spudded or completed after August 31, 1996)
options.quote: High-Cost Gas Reduced Tax Rate (Type 5) - Tax rate of 0.0 percent to 7.5 percent (.000 to .075) of the market value of gas produced from a gas well.
options.quote2: the accumulated savings statutory limitation of 50 percent of drilling and completion costs for this specific lease

code.quote: The amount of tax reduction shall be computed by subtracting from the tax rate imposed by Section 201.052 the product of that tax rate times the ratio of drilling and completion costs incurred for the well to twice the median drilling and completion costs for high-cost wells spudded or completed during the previous state fiscal year, except that the effective rate of tax may not be reduced below zero.

code2.quote: for the first 120 consecutive calendar months beginning on the first day of production, or until the cumulative value of the tax reduction equals 50 percent of the drilling and completion costs incurred for the well, whichever occurs first

options.name: Low-producing gas well credit

tiers.label: Certified average gas price more than $3.50: no credit

options.who: A gas well whose production for the prior three months averages no more than 90 Mcf per day (flared gas excluded); Form AP-217. Casinghead gas and condensate are not eligible
options.what: A credit of 25, 50 or 100 percent of the tax, set by the Comptroller-certified average (in 2005 dollars) gas price for the report month (not the price entered here). It cannot be reported with high-cost gas for the same well and period
options.how_long: Each report month, while the well qualifies and by the certified price
options.quote: Average Taxable Gas Price Credit More than $3.50 No credit Over $3 to $3.50 25 percent credit Over $2.50 to $3 50 percent credit $2.50 or less 100 percent credit

code.quote: Each month, the comptroller shall certify the average taxable price of gas, adjusted to 2005 dollars, during the previous three months

certified.note: The Comptroller-certified average taxable price by report period, in 2005 dollars, as the Comptroller's page publishes it. Rows inside an HTML comment on the page (September to December 2026, copied from 2025) are not published and are not here.

options.name: Flared Gas Exemption, Type 4
options.who: Gas from an oil well, lawfully vented or flared, certified by the Railroad Commission
options.what: 0.0 percent of market value
options.quote: Flared Gas Exemption (Type 4) - Tax rate of 0.0 percent (.000) of market value of gas produced from an oil well and lawfully vented or flared.

code.quote: The tax imposed by this chapter does not apply to gas: (1) injected into the earth in this state, unless sold for that purpose; (2) produced from oil wells with oil and lawfully vented or flared

options.name: Gas that would otherwise be vented or flared
options.who: Gas from a qualifying well consumed within 1,000 feet of the well that would otherwise have been lawfully vented or flared
options.what: 0.0 percent of market value
options.quote: consumed within 1,000 feet of the qualifying well and would otherwise have been lawfully vented or flared

code.quote: Gas produced from a qualifying well that is consumed within 1,000 feet of the qualifying well and would otherwise have been lawfully vented or flared is not subject to the tax imposed by this chapter.

options.name: Gas from certain restimulation wells, Type 17
options.who: Gas from a restimulation well certified by the Railroad Commission
options.what: 0.0 percent of market value
options.how_long: Until the earlier of the last day of the 36th consecutive month after the well first produces following the restimulation treatment, or the date the exempted taxes (chapters 201 and 202) reach the lesser of the restimulation costs or $750,000
options.quote: Exemption no longer applies once the exempted taxes for the well reach the lesser of the well's restimulation costs or $750,000.

code.quote: until the earlier of: (1) the last day of the 36th consecutive month following the month in which the well first produces hydrocarbons after a restimulation treatment is completed; or (2) the date on which the cumulative amount of taxes exempted under Chapter 201 and this chapter and any credit under Subsection (l) equals the lesser of: (A) the restimulation costs described by Subsection (j); or (B) $750,000.

options.name: Two-Year Inactive Well Exemption, Type 16
options.who: Gas from a well certified as a two-year inactive well
options.what: 0.0 percent of market value
options.how_long: Five years
options.quote: Two-Year Inactive Well Exemption (Type 16) - Tax rate of 0.0 percent (.000) of market value of gas produced from a two-year inactive well.

code.quote: Hydrocarbons produced from a well qualify for a five-year severance tax exemption if the commission designates the well as a two-year inactive well.

base.name: Condensate production tax
base.quote: Condensate Production Tax: 4.6 percent (.046) of market value of condensate.

code.quote: The tax imposed by this section is at the same rate as the rate of the tax imposed on oil by Section 202.052 of this code.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.basis_note: Oil and condensate are taxed on value at the time and place of severance: the higher of the first purchaser's gross receipts less trucking, barging and pipeline fees, or the posted field price (La. R.S. 47:633(A)(3)(a)); gas is taxed per Mcf. The transport deduction below applies to oil and condensate only.

value_deduction.label: Trucking, barging and pipeline fees, USD per bbl
value_deduction.quote: the value of oil shall be the higher of the gross receipts received from the first purchaser less charges for trucking, barging, and pipeline fees; or the posted field price

variants.label: Well completed on or after July 1, 2025

base.name: Oil severance tax
base.effective: 2025-07-01 for the 6.5 percent rate (wells completed on or after that date)
base.quote: On oil produced from a well completed before July 1, 2025, the rate of tax shall be twelve and one-half percent of its value at the time and place of severance. On oil produced from a well completed on or after July 1, 2025, the rate of tax shall be six and one-half percent

options.name: Incapable oil well
options.who: An oil well certified by the Department of Revenue as incapable of more than 25 barrels per producing day for the entire month, producing at least 50 percent salt water per day; every well on a multiple-well lease must be certified
options.what: 6.25 percent of value
options.how_long: While certified (by the 25th day of the second month after production)
options.quote: the rate of tax shall be six and one-fourth percent of its value at the time and place of severance and the well shall be defined, for severance tax purposes, as an incapable well

options.name: Stripper oil well
options.who: An oil well certified as incapable of more than 10 barrels per producing day for the entire month
options.what: 3.125 percent of value; exempt in any month the average value is below $20 per barrel
options.how_long: Until the well averages more than 10 barrels per day for an entire calendar month
options.quote: the rate of tax shall be three and one hundred twenty-five thousandths percent of its value ... Crude oil produced from certified stripper wells shall be exempt from severance tax in any month in which the average value set forth in Subparagraph (a) of this Paragraph is less than twenty dollars per barrel.

options.name: Inactive well returned to production (production commencing before October 1, 2028)
options.who: A well inactive for two years or more, or with 30 days or less of production in the past two years, certified by the Department of Conservation and Energy (applications July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2028), producing from the same interval
options.what: 3.125 percent of value (6.25 percent if production commences on or after October 1, 2028)
options.how_long: Ten years
options.quote: shall, in the case of oil, be subject to a severance tax rate of three and one hundred twenty-five thousandths percent of its value at the time and place of severance ... for a period of ten years if the production commences before October 1, 2028

options.name: Orphan well returned to production (production commencing before October 1, 2028)
options.who: A well designated an orphan well for longer than 60 months, certified by the Department of Conservation and Energy
options.what: 1.565 percent of value (3.125 percent if production commences on or after October 1, 2028)
options.how_long: Ten years
options.quote: in the case of oil, be subject to a severance tax rate of one and five hundred sixty-five thousandths percent of its value at the time and place of severance

options.name: Horizontal well exemption (FY 2027 oil price $73.28: 80 percent)
options.who: A horizontally drilled well or horizontal recompletion producing on or after July 1, 2015
options.what: 80 percent of the tax exempt for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027: the tiers run from 100 percent at $70 or less to none above $110, on the average NYMEX price the Secretary sets each July 1
options.how_long: 24 months or until payout of the well cost, whichever comes first
options.quote: Because the FY 27 average oil price is above $70 and at or below $80 per barrel , the severance tax exemption for horizontal oil wells is 80% .
options.quote2: The exemption for oil shall extend for a period of twenty-four months or until payout of the well cost is achieved, whichever comes first.

options.name: Deep well exemption
options.who: A well drilled to a true vertical depth of more than 15,000 feet, production commencing after July 31, 1994
options.what: Exempt from severance tax
options.how_long: 24 months from commercial production or until payout of the well cost, whichever comes first
options.quote: Production of natural gas, gas condensate, and oil from any well drilled to a true vertical depth of more than fifteen thousand feet, where production commences after July 31, 1994, shall, from the date commercial production begins, be exempt from severance tax for twenty-four months or until payout of the well cost, whichever comes first.

options.name: Orphan well enhancement (production commencing October 1, 2021 to June 30, 2031)
options.who: Oil from an orphan well under R.S. 30:88.2(A) enhanced under a Department of Conservation and Energy permit (re-entry, workover, plugback), certified
options.what: Exempt from severance tax; from the fourth month an amount equal to the tax is remitted to the well's site-specific trust account
options.how_long: As certified; the operator keeps the first three months' amount
options.quote: oil production from any orphan well as defined by R.S. 30:88.2(A) that is undergoing or has undergone well enhancements ... from which production commences on or after October 1, 2021, and before June 30, 2031, shall be exempt from severance tax

base.name: Natural gas severance tax
base.quote: The natural gas severance tax rate effective July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, has been set at 15.14 cents per thousand cubic feet (MCF)
base.quote2: The gas tax rate provided in Subparagraph (a) of this Paragraph shall be adjusted annually on July first for the ensuing twelve calendar months

options.name: Gas from a low-pressure oil well (50 psig or less)
options.who: Gas from a well designated an oil well with wellhead (or casinghead) pressure of 50 psig or less for the entire month; gas lift wells are presumed to qualify
options.what: 3 cents per Mcf
options.how_long: Each month the pressure test is met
options.quote: the rate shall be three cents per thousand cubic feet
options.quote2: The reduced natural gas severance tax rates provided for in La. R.S. 47:633(A)(5)(b) and (c) remain the same at 3 cents per MCF and one and three-tenths cent, respectively.

options.name: Incapable gas well (under 250,000 cubic feet per day)
options.who: A well designated a gas well, incapable of producing an average of 250,000 cubic feet per day during the entire month
options.what: 1.3 cents per Mcf
options.how_long: Each month the test is met
options.quote: the tax rate applicable to the gas severed from the well shall be one and three-tenths cents per thousand cubic feet

options.name: Inactive gas well returned to production (before October 1, 2028)
options.who: As for oil: inactive two years or more, certified, same interval
options.what: 25 percent of the gas rate: 3.785 cents per Mcf for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027
options.how_long: Ten years
options.quote: the inactive gas reduced tax rate is 3.785 cents per MCF

options.name: Orphan gas well returned to production (before October 1, 2028)
options.who: A well designated an orphan well for longer than 60 months, certified
options.what: 12.5 percent of the gas rate: 1.8925 cents per Mcf for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027
options.how_long: Ten years
options.quote: the orphan gas reduced tax rate is 1.8925 cents per MCF

options.name: Horizontal well exemption (FY 2027 gas price $3.63/MMBtu: 100 percent)
options.who: A horizontally drilled well or horizontal recompletion producing on or after July 1, 2015
options.what: 100 percent exempt for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (the tiers run from 100 percent at $4.50/MMBtu or less to none above $7)
options.how_long: 24 months or until payout for wells completed before July 1, 2025; 18 months or until payout for wells completed on or after July 1, 2025
options.quote: Because the FY 27 average natural gas price is at or below $4.50 per million BTU , the severance tax exemption for horizontal gas wells is 100%.
options.quote2: The exemption for gas produced from a well completed on or after July 1, 2025, shall extend for a period of eighteen months or until payout of the well cost is achieved, whichever comes first.

options.name: Deep well exemption
options.who: A well drilled to a true vertical depth of more than 15,000 feet, production commencing after July 31, 1994
options.what: Exempt from severance tax
options.how_long: 24 months from commercial production or until payout, whichever comes first
options.quote: shall, from the date commercial production begins, be exempt from severance tax for twenty-four months or until payout of the well cost, whichever comes first.

base.name: Severance tax on distillate, condensate or similar resources
base.quote: On distillate, condensate, or similar natural resources severed from the soil or water either with oil or gas, twelve and one-half percent of gross value at the time and place of severance.

options.name: Deep well exemption
options.who: Gas condensate from a well drilled to a true vertical depth of more than 15,000 feet, production commencing after July 31, 1994
options.what: Exempt from severance tax
options.how_long: 24 months from commercial production or until payout, whichever comes first
options.quote: Production of natural gas, gas condensate, and oil from any well drilled to a true vertical depth of more than fifteen thousand feet

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.basis_note: New Mexico's four production taxes, as the Taxation and Revenue Department names them, are levied on taxable value: in general the price at the production unit less royalties paid the United States, New Mexico or an Indian tribe or pueblo, and less reasonable trucking to the first place of market. The rates are TRD's latest published table, effective April 1, 2026 through August 31, 2026 (session 41); TRD had not published a table from September 2026 when it was read on 2026-09-30. The Oil and Gas Production Equipment Ad Valorem Tax is annual (due November 30) and is not computed.
NM.rates_as_of: TRD rate table effective 2026-04-01 through 2026-08-31 (the latest TRD has published; no table from September 2026 was found)

value_deduction.label: Royalties paid the United States, New Mexico or a tribe (percent of value) and trucking (USD per unit)
value_deduction.quote: the taxable value of products is the actual price of the product at the production unit less royalties paid the United States, the State of New Mexico or an Indian tribe or pueblo, and less the reasonable expense of trucking the product from the production unit to the first place of market

base.name: Oil and Gas Severance Tax
base.quote: KIND O, SEV 0.0375 (every county and suffix, 04/01/2026 to 08/31/2026)

base.name: Oil and Gas Emergency School Tax
Oil and Gas Ad Valorem Production Tax

input.label: Your production unit's county, district and suffix

base.quote: This is an ad valorem tax on the assessed value of products severed and sold from each production unit. The assessed value is determined by applying the uniform assessment ratio to the taxable value of products.

districts.note: The column AD /2 of TRD's table: SEV + SCHOOL + CONS + AD /2 equals its Total Rate on every row, so AD /2 is the production ad valorem rate (the table's AD VAL, twice it, is the equipment tax)
